items.title: Tuanku Muhriz's return from overseas to draw attention amid Negri Sembilan throne dispute
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The return of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from overseas tonight is expected to draw attention amid an ongoing dispute over the state's throne. Tuanku Muhriz is scheduled to arrive at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Sepang at 8.30pm. Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today confirmed that a proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan had been approved.

items.title: Impoverished by war in Iran, Afghan migrants return to Taliban rule
items.summary: The family came back nearly empty-handed, Saeed said. "The Iranian currency had fallen so sharply," he said, that the family's savings, held in Iranian rials, lost over two-thirds of their value. Now, Iran's economy has collapsed so severely that many Afghans said they saw returning as their only option.

items.title: Rauf: DAP's choice whether they want to contest 10 or 20 seats
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: It is up to DAP to choose the number of seats to contest in the Melaka election, says Chief Minister and state Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. He said he had no right to stop any party from voicing their intentions to contest any seat. Rauf said, on an open political stage, every party has the right to decide on its own stand and strategy.

items.title: Vodus study puts Anwar ahead of PM hopefuls with highest acceptance and first-choice support
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emerged as the strongest overall candidate for the prime ministership in a new national study by Vodus Research, recording the highest public acceptance, first-choice support and net acceptance among five prominent prospective candidates. The Malaysia Prime Minister Candidate Study 2026 found that 46 per cent of respondents aware of the candidates said they would accept Anwar as prime minister, while 34 per cent named him as their first choice. His net acceptance score stood at +19 percentage points, also the highest among the five candidates surveyed.

items.title: MASkargo, IAG & Qatar Airways Cargo complete trial ahead of JV launch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MAB Kargo Sdn Bhd (MASkargo), IAG Cargo and Qatar Airways Cargo have completed the trial of the first customer shipment transported across all three carriers. This is ahead of the full launch of their global cargo joint business later this year. Announced in 2025, the global cargo joint business brings together three leading cargo carriers to create a network of unprecedented scale and reach.

items.title: Court grants GISBH-linked businessman DNAA in intimidation case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The magistrates' court today granted businessman Mohamad Riza Makar, who is linked to Global Ikhwan Service and Business Holdings (GISBH), a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in an intimidation case. The decision came after deputy public prosecutor Faizah Khalilah Zaberi told magistrate Irza Zulaikha Rohanuddin that the prosecution wanted to review the case further. "However, she failed to appear on both occasions," said Boestamam.

items.title: 12-year-old faces possible PwD registration after alleged bullying leaves her near paralysis
items.summary: Her mother, Norasikin Hasin, 32, said the hospital recently issued a confirmation letter to facilitate the registration of her eldest daughter following a deterioration in her physical condition. Norasikin said she was torn over whether to proceed with the registration as her daughter was born healthy and had grown up actively like other children. Norasikin said her daughter had been unable to attend school for almost eight months since the incident in February due to her health condition.

items.title: North Korea says US-led arms buildup justifies expanding nuclear force
items.summary: BEIJING: North Korea's vice defence minister said on Thursday that a growing US-led military buildup and what he called an expanding nuclear alliance among Washington, Seoul and Tokyo justified Pyongyang's efforts to strengthen and expand its nuclear forces. Speaking at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, China's flagship international security conference, Vice Defence Minister Kim Kang Il said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was irreversible and pledged to continue expanding its nuclear arsenal. "The ceaseless nuclear arms buildup of the enemy states fully justifies the building of a solid nuclear shield of the DPRK," Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea's formal name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.

items.title: High Court sets Nov 6 mention for Rosmah solar appeal update
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: High Court proceedings to record additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case appeal have been postponed. The deferment follows the Court of Appeal's decision today to allow the prosecution's application to stay execution of its Sept 1 order pending an appeal to the Federal Court. He said the Court of Appeal had set Oct 7 for case management via e-Review to track the status of the Federal Court appeal, while vacating the main appeal hearing originally scheduled for October.

items.title: Army steps up drone surveillance on border routes amid unrest in southern Thailand
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) is using advanced drone technology to strengthen security monitoring in hard-to-reach areas along the Malaysia-Thailand border, particularly in response to the unrest in southern Thailand. Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the technology enabled TDM to overcome the challenges posed by hilly and densely forested terrain, where physical patrols by troops were difficult. Azhan also gave an assurance that border security remained tight, with round-the-clock operations in place.

items.title: 43 countries call on Taliban to lift 'suffocating restrictions' on Afghan women
items.summary: NEW YORK: More than 40 countries on Wednesday called on the Taliban government to immediately remove all restrictions on the rights of women and girls in Afghanistan. Last month marked five years since the Taliban returned to power and imposed what the UN called "suffocating restrictions" on Afghans, especially women. Around 2.4 million Afghan girls and young women are currently deprived of secondary education, according to Unesco.

items.title: Loke: Negri exco members should resign if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan executive council (exco) members should step down if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state's Yang di-Pertuan Besar, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said. Loke said all the exco members concerned had only recently taken their oaths of office before Tuanku Muhriz early last month. He said an exco decision could not, by itself, override the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959 or the decisions of the Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.

items.title: Japan's Takaichi keeps key ministers in cabinet reshuffle
items.summary: TOKYO: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi retained her key ministers on Thursday in a cabinet reshuffle aimed at solidifying the ruling coalition and advancing a food tax cut despite concerns over how it will be financed. They include Kihara, finance minister Satsuki Katayama, foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi. The prime minister also retained key economic ministers, including trade and industry minister Ryosei Akazawa, who has led Japan's tariff negotiations with the United States, and economic growth strategy minister Minoru Kiuchi, who favours active fiscal spending.

items.title: 102-year-old Tok Saimah shares secrets to long, healthy life
items.summary: KLUANG: At 102, Saimah Sajiman still follows the simple routines that have shaped her life, particularly when it comes to her diet and regular meal times. More fondly known as Tok Saimah, the centenarian from Kampung Rahmat, Sri Lalang, believes that maintaining a healthy diet, particularly choosing boiled food over fried or oily dishes, is among the practices that have helped her stay healthy. Lunch is before Zohor prayer and dinner is before Isyak prayer," she said.

items.title: Give parents a middle ground on haze absences, say parents, school groups
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parents and school community leaders want the Education Ministry to have a middle ground option when it comes to keeping their children home because of the haze. While Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has said parents may keep children home during haze without penalty, they said this still left parents choosing between their children's health and education. He also said there should be clearer communication from schools on Air Pollutant Index readings and learning arrangements.

items.title: KLIA ranks first in Asia for connectivity in OAG Megahubs 2026 ranking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) ranked fourth globally and first among all Asian airports in OAG’s Megahubs 2026 ranking, with connections to 154 destinations, while also topping the Low-Cost Carrier (LCC) Megahubs index with nearly 15,000 possible low-cost connections. OAG, the intelligence partner for global travel, said its annual ranking of global airport connectivity showed Asia Pacific (APAC) dominating the index, with eight airports in the global top 20. According to OAG in a statement, AirAsia operates 34 per cent of total flights at KUL, while Seoul Incheon ranked second in the LCC rankings with connectivity reaching 198 destinations.

items.title: Buckingham Palace hits back at claims in Princess Diana book
items.summary: LONDON: Buckingham Palace has hit back at claims by the late Princess Diana's brother that King Charles III acted insensitively following her death in a car crash almost 30 years ago. The palace issued an unusually strong statement after Charles Spencer claimed in his new memoir that the then-prince, Diana's former husband, said "rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough" days after she died in 1997. '," Spencer writes.

items.title: Malacca Strait cable disruption could cripple key services across the region
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Beneath the Strait of Malacca, one of the world's busiest shipping routes, lie strategically critical submarine cables transmitting US$10 trillion in financial transactions daily, with any serious disruption potentially crippling banks, hospitals and airports in Malaysia and across the region. Citizens International chairman Dr Shahridan Faiez, who is also Technical Director at Think City and previously worked with the World Bank, said the submarine cables added another critical dimension to the strategic importance of the waterway, which is already a major conduit for global trade and energy supplies. On the possibility of diverting shipping through the Lombok and Makassar straits if the Strait of Malacca were seriously disrupted, Shahridan said such an option was not realistic, given the significant difference in vessel traffic and the lack of necessary infrastructure.

items.title: Room view complaint escalates into assault at Bukit Bintang hotel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A China tourist's request to change her hotel room over its view turned chaotic after she claimed she was assaulted and injured by a local married couple in the hotel lobby in Bukit Bintang here yesterday. According to her account, the request was rejected by hotel staff, who she claimed also appeared displeased. The source said the woman subsequently lodged a police report following the incident.

items.title: Cleaning supervisor charged with robbing, injuring four Rohingya men
items.summary: Muhammad Haziq Mohd Rizar, 26, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before judges N. Kanageswari and Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim, as well as magistrate A. Shaarmini. For the first to third charges, the accused allegedly robbed three men who are United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders. The offences were allegedly committed in Jalan Pekaka 3 and Jalan Pekaka 5, Taman Perling, here at 1.50pm and 2.30pm on Aug 26, and at a playground in Jalan Layang 12, Taman Perling, at 10am on Sept 9.

items.title: UN mission finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran
items.summary: GENEVA: A UN fact-finding mission on Iran said on Thursday it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States was behind two military strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February, and that these constituted war crimes. US officials have previously said military operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict, while Iran has consistently rejected allegations of systematic rights violations. The UN experts said they found reasonable grounds to believe US forces were responsible for an attack on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the city of Minab, where more than 150 people were killed, including around 120 schoolchildren, according to Iranian officials.

items.title: New MyKad pitched as fix for subsidy leakages
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The new MyKad could help address long-standing problems in Malaysia's subsidy system by enabling beneficiaries to be verified in real time, according to its developr NexG Bhd. The technology group said the new identity card combines biometric QR verification with an optional digital eWallet, allowing identity, authentication and payments to be linked through a single credential. The company said the MyKad's biometric QR capability could also complement MyDigital ID by providing an additional layer of identity verification, subject to technical integration and approvals.

items.title: Tuan Ibrahim: Public interest warrants continued push on Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas will continue to raise issues concerning the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), including during next month's Dewan Rakyat sitting. "The TH RCI issue will continue to be raised. podcast broadcast yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said TH itself had requested the government to postpone disclosing the RCI findings when they were completed in 2022.

items.title: Lorry attendant gets one-year jail for spying on bathing stepdaughter, 12
items.summary: Under the section, the accused could have been sentenced to up to five years in jail, a fine or both. "The court took into account the relationship between the accused and the victim before handing down the sentence of a year's jail, taking effect from the date of arrest (Sept 10)," said Mustakim. The accused was arrested at 5.47pm the next day.

items.title: Ketamine-positive woman arrested after swinging a knife at police
items.summary: Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police attempted to arrest the woman at 3.45pm. "During the arrest, the suspect acted aggressively by grabbing a knife and attacking police officers," he said in a statement today. Rosdi said preliminary urine screening showed that the suspect tested positive for ketamine.

items.title: Kota Kinabalu airport runway temporarily closed for rectification works
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today. In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure. “The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.

items.title: Prosecution gets stay on hearing additional evidence in Rosmah's solar trial
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution's application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case. "With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal's order dated Sept 1 until the prosecution's appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court. "We hope the parties will inform the High Court of the Federal Court's decision as soon as it is delivered to facilitate case management at the High Court.

items.title: Buzze Azam fails to overturn RM15,000 fine over Facebook post
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyer Mohd Khairul Azam Abdul Aziz, also known as Buzze Azam, has failed to overturn his conviction and RM15,000 fine over an offensive Facebook post criticising the criminal justice system. High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin dismissed Khairul Azam's appeals against both his conviction and sentence, as well as the prosecution's appeal for a heavier sentence. Khairul Azam had been charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 over a Facebook post published on March 24, 2021.

items.title: Malaysia's fiscal deficit seen narrowing in 2027: JP Morgan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027, from a projected 3.5 per cent this year, according to JP Morgan. The US investment bank said the government was balancing near-term support measures with increasingly binding medium-term fiscal constraints. JP Morgan said the government has progressively reduced the deficit from 6.4 per cent of GDP in 2021 to 3.7 per cent in 2025 via a mix of revenue enhancing and expenditure reducing measures.

items.title: Papagomo fails to stay RM280,000 defamation payout to Lim Guan Eng, son
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son. On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020. The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).

items.title: Palm oil mill shut down after pump failure sends effluent into Johor’s Sungai Sembrong
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately. “Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong. The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.

items.title: BPHB unit appointed Bintulu Port operator for 30 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056. “The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.

items.title: Kepong restaurant assault: Technician seeks lesser charge through A-GC representation
items.summary: Lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin, who represents Lai Kae Bin, 33, said the representation was submitted on Sept 2 for a review of the charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code. Firdaus said Lai had instructed him to seek a lesser charge, as he felt the existing charge was too serious. Lai is one of three men charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to businessman Andrew Teh, 47, using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong at 2am on May 7.

items.title: PMO says letter claiming Cabinet approval for PLUS highway widening is fake
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake. In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval. “PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.

items.title: Zulkifli: People of faith should not mock or insult other religions
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Verse 11 of Surah Al-Hujurat clearly forbids believers from insulting fellow human beings, mocking, calling each other by bad nicknames, and denouncing one another. Noorazli's joke angered many people, with one minister calling for him to be investigated . Meanwhile, when met after a function at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Zulkifli said anything which went against religious values should be rejected.

items.title: Gas Malaysia teams up with France's Air Liquide on low-carbon energy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gas Malaysia Bhd has teamed up with France's Air Liquide Engineering & Construction to explore opportunities in low-carbon hydrogen, carbon dioxide off-take and bio-liquefied natural gas in Malaysia. The two companies will assess potential projects combining Gas Malaysia's market reach and gas infrastructure with Air Liquide's expertise in industrial gas technologies and engineering. Gas Malaysia president and group chief executive officer Azli Mohamed said the collaboration was part of the company's efforts to expand beyond conventional gas supply into renewable gas, hydrogen and other lower-carbon industrial solutions.

items.title: Critics of Anwar should back their words with action, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions. He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people. “Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.

items.title: Zahid arrives in Jakarta for 4-day working visit
items.summary: JAKARTA: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi arrived here for a working visit aimed at strengthening Malaysia-Indonesia cooperation in disaster management, including forest and land fires, as well as the halal industry and rural development. Zahid arrived at Halim Perdanakusuma International Airport here at 1.15pm local time and was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador-designate to Indonesia Datuk Muzaffar Shah Mustafa, head of Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) Ahmad Haikal Hasan and Indonesian officials. Gibran is expected to be accompanied by Home Affairs Minister Muhammad Tito Karnavian, Marine Affairs and Fisheries Minister Sakti Wahyu Trenggono, Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Minister Yandri Susanto and Environment Minister Mohamad Jumhur Hidayat.

items.title: Indonesia to begin e-commerce tax collection from Oct 1, media reports
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia will begin making e-commerce platforms collect income taxes from sellers starting Oct 1, a month earlier than previously announced, local media reported on Thursday, citing the tax chief. The move reverses a delay ordered by the previous finance minister and follows a shake-up at the top of the finance ministry this week. The finance ministry and the tax office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: Melaka assembly dissolution date still undecided, says CM
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved. The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31.

items.title: Court of Appeal stays Rosmah’s additional evidence hearing pending Federal Court appeal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution’s application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s corruption case involving the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project. “With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal’s order dated September 1 until the prosecution’s appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court. On September 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.

items.title: Quit if you no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz as ruler, Loke tells Negeri Sembilan exco members
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 17 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook today called on Negeri Sembilan executive council members to resign if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar. Yesterday, the state Exco announced that it regarded an April 19 proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz from the throne as valid and recognised Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar with immediate effect. Loke said Tuanku Muhriz could not be removed from the throne without going through the process required under the state constitution.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB instructs state secretary to gazette Tuanku Muhriz’s removal despite DKU objection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has instructed the state secretary to proceed with gazetting the removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, despite the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) saying the state executive council has no jurisdiction to determine the ruler’s position. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT) Ismail told reporters after an event in Seremban that he endorsed the statement issued by the state executive council yesterday affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal. The exco’s statement yesterday affirmed that Tuanku Muhriz’s removal in April was legitimate and that Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Kedah fertiliser company managing director released on MACC bail
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in Kedah has released the managing director of a fertiliser supplier company who was remanded in connection with the delay in the distribution of Supplementary Compound Fertiliser supplies to paddy farmers in the state. Meanwhile, Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong, when contacted, confirmed the matter and said the suspect had been released on MACC bail. Previously, the MACC opened an investigation paper regarding the issue of delayed distribution of Paddy Fertiliser 3 to paddy farmers in Kedah.

items.title: Global energy shock now hitting Malaysia’s electricity costs, says economy minister
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 17 — Global energy supply disruptions are now exhibiting a lagging effect, as the impact, concentrated on the petrol market since last March, begins to spread to natural gas and coal. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the lagging effect is beginning to impact electricity generation costs directly, particularly for consumers whose monthly electricity usage exceeds 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh). “Natural gas is a fuel that is burned to generate energy.

items.title: First recipients praise new MyKad’s tougher security and sturdier design
items.summary: Nineteen-year-old student Puteri Nur Syafiqah Jailani said she was excited to receive the new-generation MyKad on the first day of its issuance, describing the replacement process at NRD as easy and fast. “Actually, I did not know that the new MyKad would be issued today. When I arrived at NRD, I saw a notice about the new MyKad.

items.title: Soldier charged with kicking five-year-old daughter at Kelantan eatery
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 17 — A soldier was charged in the Sessions Court here today with abusing his five-year-old daughter by kicking her at an eatery in Jalan Kuala Krai last Friday. According to the charge, the accused allegedly kicked the girl at an eatery at Lot 143, Batu 2, Jalan Kuala Krai, here at 10.55pm on September 11, 2026. Earlier, the prosecution did not offer bail, citing concerns that the accused could interfere with the victim, who is also his biological daughter.

items.title: Puchong blaze guts four factories, collapse risk remains (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A fire destroyed four factories at Jalan TPP 5/15, Puchong Industrial Park, today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 6.34am. He said the fire affected a total area measuring 80 by 100 feet, involving four premises comprising a tyre factory, a hardware factory for pipes and valves, a furniture factory and an engineering factory.

items.title: BUDI Diesel mobile counters proposed for Sabah, Sarawak, says minister
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) mobile counter programme has been proposed for expansion to Sabah and Sarawak to ensure rural and remote communities are not left out of the initiative’s enhanced benefits because of limited access to digital services. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the geographical realities of both states required an approach that brought services closer to the people rather than relying solely on online platforms. The geographical realities of Sabah and Sarawak, particularly for rural and remote communities, call for a more direct, hands-on approach.

items.title: Bill requiring children to support ageing parents likely next year, says Kulasegaran
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — The proposed filial law that would legally require children to care for their ageing parents is still under consultation and is likely to be tabled early next year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said. Kulasegaran said he had hoped the Bill could be tabled by October this year, but the timeframe was too short as the government still needed to consult non-governmental organisations, relevant departments and other stakeholders. He said Malaysia had studied similar laws in countries including Singapore and India, where legislation allows parents who are not supported by their children to seek a court order requiring their children to provide financial support.

items.title: Kuantan businessman loses RM218,000 after 53 transactions in crypto scam
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 17 — A senior citizen lost RM218,239.24 after he was believed to have fallen victim to a non-existent cryptocurrency investment scam advertised on social media. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the 65-year-old man, who runs a water filter business in Kuantan, came across a cryptocurrency investment offer on Facebook before joining a WhatsApp group last July. “The victim was then given instructions to make an investment and was promised high returns based on the profits displayed through the Uphold application,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz remains legitimate Yamtuan, says Negeri Sembilan DKU
items.summary: It said such matters fell outside the jurisdiction of the state executive council and contradicted the binding determinations of the DKU under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution. The statement came after two statements were issued following the DKU’s September 13 media statement, namely the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar’s statement dated September 15 and the document titled “Keputusan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan Bil. It said this position was consistent with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and the DKU’s own determinations.

items.title: Sabah Marine Police seize untaxed cigarettes, liquor worth RM5.37m
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The Region 4 Sabah Marine Police (PPM) seized untaxed cigarettes and liquor worth nearly RM5.37 million in three raids in Sandakan and Kota Kinabalu early this week. In a statement today, Region 4 Sabah PPM said the first raid was conducted at an unregistered jetty along the Seguntur River in Sandakan at about 1.30 am on Sept 15 as part of a special joint operation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), following intelligence gathering. An inspection of the boat uncovered 1.73 million sticks of cigarettes of various brands, with an estimated seizure value of RM2.326 million.

items.title: Masked gang steals up to RM1m in second robbery at Kedah goldsmith
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Sept 17 — Four masked men armed with hammers and sharp weapons robbed a goldsmith shop in Bakar Arang here yesterday, making off with jewellery worth between RM700,000 and RM1 million. Kuala Muda Police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said police received a call at 7.20 pm alerting them to the incident at the shop located inside a supermarket here. Two of them entered the shop while the other two waited outside.

items.title: Perak worst hit as 28 areas nationwide turn unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A total of 28 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9.45am today. In Kuala Lumpur, unhealthy readings were recorded in Cheras (157) and Batu Muda (155), while Putrajaya recorded 157. In addition, 32 areas nationwide recorded readings at moderate levels, while eight areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Police probe 14-year-old driver after he crashes into two cars in Perai
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 17 — Police have confirmed a viral video showing a 14-year-old boy driving a car and crashing into two vehicles at two separate locations in Taman Chai Leng, Perai, here. “Preliminary investigations found that the teenager, who was driving from Lorong Kurau 23 towards Jalan Kurau 1, first crashed into a car parked on the road shoulder. “He then continued driving before allegedly entering the wrong side of a one-way road at Lebuh Kurau 5 and crashing into another car travelling in the correct lane,” he said in a statement last night.

items.title: Health Ministry denies claims officials absent from funerals of FDS crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Allegations that no senior health officials attended the funerals of members of the Flying Doctors Service (FDS) killed in a crash in Sarawak are untrue and irresponsible, Health deputy director-general Dr Ismuni Bohari said. He added that he himself had visited the families of the crash victims in Miri and Kuching, and also paid his last respects to the victims. “I myself was there, visiting the victims’ families in Miri and Kuching on behalf of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad and the ministry’s senior leaders and paid my last respects to my beloved FDS colleagues.

items.title: Malaysians in Saudi Arabia told to remain calm, follow instructions amid emergency alerts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Malaysians who receive alerts through Saudi Arabia’s National Early Warning Platform are advised to remain calm, stay vigilant and strictly follow instructions issued by Saudi authorities. The Consulate General of Malaysia in Jeddah also advised Malaysians to take appropriate safety precautions upon receiving an emergency alert. Malaysians who require emergency consular assistance can contact the consulate general at +966 57 309 9589.

items.title: MCA ready for GE16, focus not on number of seats, says Wee
items.summary: YONG PENG, Sept 17 — MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong yesterday declared that the party is at a high level of readiness to face the 16th general election (GE16). The Ayer Hitam MP said MCA has been preparing early to face the election and did not leave things to the last minute, adding that elections could be called at any time because administrations usually last between three years eight months and over four years, based on the last 15 general elections. Maybe four to five months.

items.title: Sarawak gets RM1.5b interim special grant as talks continue on annual formula, says Anwar
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday announced an increase in Sarawak’s interim special grant to RM1.5 billion, up from RM600 million previously, effective this year. He said the Federal Government will continue negotiations with the Sabah and Sarawak state governments to finalise a sustainable formula for determining the annual Special Grant rate. Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
